text: We will continue to develop Plaid Cymru’s Inspire Wales programme to involve all ages in sporting activity and ensure our people stay fit and healthy.
explanation: Straightforward programme commitment (sports participation for fitness and health) with purely instrumental language and no moral vocabulary; matches the codebook's negative example almost verbatim.

text: Values of respect.
explanation: Explicit invocation of a moral value — 'respect' is listed in the codebook's definition as a core moral concept. Even in fragmentary form, it affirms a normative value rather than describing a policy instrument.

text: • Waiting lists are not tolerable.
explanation: Uses explicit moral-evaluative vocabulary: the codebook lists 'tolerable/intolerable' as moral evaluation language. Declaring waiting lists 'not tolerable' is a normative judgment of wrongness, not an administrative target.

text: to ensure an efficient and accessible school bus system for communities across the country.
explanation: A neutral description of a policy goal (efficient, accessible school bus system). 'Efficient' and 'accessible' are instrumental criteria, not moral vocabulary; equality-of-access framed instrumentally is coded 0 per the negative clarification.

text: work with stakeholders to ensure ticket prices at sporting events do not unfairly discriminate against people from low socio economic backgrounds.
explanation: Contains explicit moral vocabulary: 'unfairly discriminate' invokes both fairness ('unfair') and discrimination, which the codebook lists as moral concepts. The policy commitment is framed as preventing a moral wrong.

text: Much of the UK’s language, culture and way of life has been enriched by successive new arrivals over thousands of years.
explanation: A descriptive positive claim about immigration's contribution ('enriched' language, culture, way of life). 'Enriched' is a generic positive adjective without explicit moral-evaluative vocabulary such as justice, rights, or desert.

text: The international evidence is clear:
explanation: A neutral empirical framing ('the international evidence is clear'); appeals to evidence rather than to moral values or normative judgments.

text: and free prescriptions and eye tests for the over-60s, without means testing.
explanation: A neutral description of a policy instrument (free prescriptions and eye tests, no means testing). No moral vocabulary; entitlement design framed administratively.

text: In government, The Nationals will place any money left in this program in the hands of school boards and principals who are best placed to know how and where the priorities for their schools lie.
explanation: Administrative allocation of programme funds to school boards and principals; instrumental reasoning about who is 'best placed' to set priorities, with no moral-evaluative language.

text: Revive the National Adult Learning Council and local co-ordinating bodies so that diverse elements of lifelong learning can be linked into one coherent system through which learners can progress.
explanation: Institutional/administrative proposal (revive a council and co-ordinating bodies for lifelong learning). No moral vocabulary, purely programmatic.

text: And as I’ve mentioned, as a result of our initiative, the Three Strikes legislation was passed.
explanation: Factual claim that legislation was passed as a result of an initiative; a descriptive achievement statement with no moral evaluation.

text: and stop unions looking to restrict their freedom to choose how they want to work.
explanation: Appeals to 'freedom to choose how they want to work' as a value being unjustly restricted (by unions). The codebook's clarification explicitly includes appeals to freedom/liberty being protected or unjustly restricted.

text: Every person, however frail or vulnerable, has a place and a purpose in this world.
explanation: Matches the codebook's positive example: affirms the inherent worth of every human being 'however frail or vulnerable' — a direct moral claim about human dignity and purpose.

text: Ensure that all children will be tested in literacy and numeracy at two stages during their primary school education.
explanation: A neutral policy instrument (testing children in literacy and numeracy). Administrative/educational target with no moral-evaluative language.

text: - We have one court system
explanation: Descriptive statement of institutional fact ('we have one court system'); no moral vocabulary or normative judgment.

text: Many new small businesses are started by women.

text: Our economy will be thriving, delivering balanced growth with jobs that last in every nation and region.

explanation: Purely instrumental fragment about contributing technology; no moral content.

text: · further support for back country reafforestation.
